In the diagram, $Q$ lies on the segment $MF$. The given vectors are $\overrightarrow{OM}=n$ and $\overrightarrow{OF}=d$. The lengths satisfy $MQ:QF=1:1$.

Express $\overrightarrow{OQ}$ in terms of $n$ and $d$. Fill in both coefficients, including their signs.

$\overrightarrow{OQ}=$ {{field-1}} $n+$ {{field-2}} $d$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First express both endpoint vectors in the directions away from $O$:

$$
\overrightarrow{OM}=n\qquad \overrightarrow{OF}=d .
$$

Trace the path from $M$ through $O$ to $F$:

$$
\overrightarrow{MF}=\overrightarrow{MO}+\overrightarrow{OF}=-n+d.
$$

The ratio $MQ:QF=1:1$ gives $2$ parts in the whole segment. Thus

$$
\overrightarrow{MQ}=\frac{1}{2}\overrightarrow{MF}=\frac{1}{2}(-n+d).
$$

Add along the path $O\to M\to Q$ and collect coefficients:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{OQ}&=\overrightarrow{OM}+\overrightarrow{MQ}\\&=n+\frac{1}{2}(-n+d)\\&=\frac{1}{2}n+\frac{1}{2}d.\end{aligned}
$$

In the diagram, $D$ lies on the segment $KM$. The given vectors are $\overrightarrow{OK}=k$ and $\overrightarrow{OM}=v$. The lengths satisfy $KD:DM=1:2$.

Express $\overrightarrow{OD}$ in terms of $k$ and $v$. Fill in both coefficients, including their signs.

$\overrightarrow{OD}=$ {{field-1}} $k+$ {{field-2}} $v$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First express both endpoint vectors in the directions away from $O$:

$$
\overrightarrow{OK}=k\qquad \overrightarrow{OM}=v .
$$

Trace the path from $K$ through $O$ to $M$:

$$
\overrightarrow{KM}=\overrightarrow{KO}+\overrightarrow{OM}=-k+v.
$$

The ratio $KD:DM=1:2$ gives $3$ parts in the whole segment. Thus

$$
\overrightarrow{KD}=\frac{1}{3}\overrightarrow{KM}=\frac{1}{3}(-k+v).
$$

Add along the path $O\to K\to D$ and collect coefficients:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{OD}&=\overrightarrow{OK}+\overrightarrow{KD}\\&=k+\frac{1}{3}(-k+v)\\&=\frac{2}{3}k+\frac{1}{3}v.\end{aligned}
$$

In the diagram, $L$ lies on the segment $XW$. The given vectors are $\overrightarrow{OX}=c$ and $\overrightarrow{OW}=d$. The lengths satisfy $XL:LW=4:5$.

Express $\overrightarrow{OL}$ in terms of $c$ and $d$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First express both endpoint vectors in the directions away from $O$:

$$
\overrightarrow{OX}=c\qquad \overrightarrow{OW}=d .
$$

Trace the path from $X$ through $O$ to $W$:

$$
\overrightarrow{XW}=\overrightarrow{XO}+\overrightarrow{OW}=-c+d.
$$

The ratio $XL:LW=4:5$ gives $9$ parts in the whole segment. Thus

$$
\overrightarrow{XL}=\frac{4}{9}\overrightarrow{XW}=\frac{4}{9}(-c+d).
$$

Add along the path $O\to X\to L$ and collect coefficients:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{OL}&=\overrightarrow{OX}+\overrightarrow{XL}\\&=c+\frac{4}{9}(-c+d)\\&=\frac{5}{9}c+\frac{4}{9}d.\end{aligned}
$$

In the diagram, $X$ lies on the segment $YQ$. The given vectors are $\overrightarrow{OY}=e$ and $\overrightarrow{OQ}=g$. The lengths satisfy $YX:XQ=4:1$.

Express $\overrightarrow{OX}$ in terms of $e$ and $g$. Fill in both coefficients, including their signs.

$\overrightarrow{OX}=$ {{field-1}} $e+$ {{field-2}} $g$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First express both endpoint vectors in the directions away from $O$:

$$
\overrightarrow{OY}=e\qquad \overrightarrow{OQ}=g .
$$

Trace the path from $Y$ through $O$ to $Q$:

$$
\overrightarrow{YQ}=\overrightarrow{YO}+\overrightarrow{OQ}=-e+g.
$$

The ratio $YX:XQ=4:1$ gives $5$ parts in the whole segment. Thus

$$
\overrightarrow{YX}=\frac{4}{5}\overrightarrow{YQ}=\frac{4}{5}(-e+g).
$$

Add along the path $O\to Y\to X$ and collect coefficients:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{OX}&=\overrightarrow{OY}+\overrightarrow{YX}\\&=e+\frac{4}{5}(-e+g)\\&=\frac{1}{5}e+\frac{4}{5}g.\end{aligned}
$$
